title: Western Blotting Protocol
author: Mannan Nouri
materials: Treat cells with drug, or transfection reagents according to manufacturer’s instructions. Note: Serum starve and treat for 30 minutes for phosphorylation targets, and treat for 24-96 hours with our without starvation for other targets.
Prepare chemiluminescence reagents (Fisher, #509049325) in a container large enough to fit membrane(s).
Incubate the membranes in chemiluminescence reagents for 1 minute with gentle agitation. Note: Do not stack membranes in container, or allow them to contact the protein side of any other membrane(s).

steps.title: Dissociate and pellet cells
steps.instruction: Dissociate adherent cells using 0.25% Trypsin (Fisher, #MT25053CI) for 5-10 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Deactivate Trypsin using 10% Fetal Bovine Serum/FBS (Fisher, #SH3007203) or 10% Charcoal Stripped Serum/CSS (Fisher, #SH3006803) media.
Pellet cells at 1500 RPM.

steps.title: Count and seed cells
steps.instruction: Re-suspend cells in culture medium and determine cell count.

substeps.instruction: Count cells using Trypan Blue Solution (Fisher, #MT-25-900-CI) and a manual or electronic Hemacytometer.
Seed cells equally into individual wells of a 6-Well plate.
Allow cells to attach for 24-48 hours.

steps.title: Harvest protein
steps.instruction: Harvest protein from cells using RIPA buffer.

substeps.instruction: Wash cells gently with 1X PBS (Fisher, #4054-1012).

Scrape cells and transfer to a 1.5mL Eppendorf tube using a p200 pipette in 120µL of RIPA (Fisher, #89901) supplemented with phosphatase inhibitor (Fisher, #78426) and protease inhibitor (Fisher, #78439).

steps.title: Lyse and clear samples
steps.instruction: Incubate and centrifuge samples to remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Incubate samples for 30 minutes at 4°C to allow lysis (alternatively, store lysates at -20°C).
Spin down samples at max RPM at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Remove debris pellet with a p20 pipette tip or transfer supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Quantify and prepare protein samples
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration and prepare for loading.

substeps.instruction: Conduct Bicinchoninic Acid (BCA) analysis (Fisher, #PI23225) according to manufacturer's instructions.
Dilute all samples in RIPA and 4X Laemmli buffer (BioRad, #1610747) to a total volume of 100µL at 1µg/µL, adding β-Mercaptoethanol to Laemmli immediately before use.

steps.title: Denature proteins
steps.instruction: Heat samples to denature proteins based on protein type.

substeps.instruction: For most proteins: Heat for 5 minutes at 95°C.
For heat-sensitive, membrane proteins, or to preserve interactions: Heat for 10 minutes at 65°C.

steps.title: Prepare gel and load samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the electrophoresis apparatus and load the protein samples.

substeps.instruction: Prepare gel apparatus using 10x Tris/Glycine/SDS running buffer (Bio-Rad, #1610772).
Wash gel wells with running buffer using a gel loading tip (USA Scientific, #1022-0600) to remove storage buffer.
Load samples onto BioRad pre-cast 4-20% 15-Well gradient gels (#4561093EDU) using a gel loading tip.

Ensure all wells have the same volume (e.g., 10µL) using loading buffer and β-Mercaptoethanol to top up discordant volumes (e.g., 6µL Loading Buffer and 4µL Precision Plus Dual Color Ladder [BioRad, #1610394]).

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel at constant current.

substeps.instruction: Run at 5 milliamps constant per gel for 30 minutes to allow samples to enter the gel.
Run at 10-50 milliamps constant until the dye front leaves the gel or desired separation is achieved.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer the gel to a nitrocellulose membrane.

substeps.instruction: Use the BioRad Trans-Blot Turbo Transfer system with the Trans-Blot Turbo RTA Mini 0-2 um Nitrocellulose Transfer Kit (#1704270).
Follow manufacturer's instructions (typically 1.3amps and 25 volts for 7 minutes for mixed molecular weight targets).

steps.title: Block membranes
steps.instruction: Block the membrane to prevent non-specific binding.

substeps.instruction: Immediately after transfer, block membranes for 60 minutes on a shaker in 5% milk (Fisher, #NC9121673) in 1X Tris Buffered Saline (BioRad, #1706435) plus 0.1% Tween20 (Sigma-Aldrich, P1379-500ML) (TBS-T).
Note: Use 5% BSA TBS-T for detection of phosphorylated-proteins.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Probe the membrane with the primary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Wash whole or sectioned membranes with TBS-T to remove milk.
Incubate membranes overnight on a shaker at 4°C with primary antibody diluted in 5% BSA (Fisher, AM2616) in TBS-T (Alternatively: probe for one hour at room temperature).

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Probe the membrane with the secondary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Wash membranes with TBS-T three times for a total of 15 minutes.
Incubate membranes for one hour on a shaker at 4°C with secondary antibody diluted in 5% Milk/BSA TBS-T.
Note: Cover membranes to protect from light if using fluorescent secondary antibodies.

steps.title: Final washes and imaging
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane and expose for signal detection.

substeps.instruction: Wash membranes with TBS-T three times for a total of 15 minutes (Note: fluorescent antibodies may go directly to imaging in Li-Cor Odyssey or other imager).
Place membranes protein side up on a Kimwipe (Fisher, 06666A) to blot excess buffer and allow to dry for 1-3 minutes (do not blot protein side or allow to fully dry).
Expose membranes using film (Research Products International Corp, #248300) or electronic imagers (BioRad/Licor).
Wash membranes with TBS-T two times to remove chemiluminescence reagents.
Store membranes at 4°C in TBS (not TBS-T), or re-probe for other targets immediately.
